name: Butternut Squash
description: Butternut squash (Cucurbita moschata) is a highly nutrient-dense winter vegetable, prized for its complex starch matrix and concentrated carotenoid profile. It serves as an essential botanical source of provitamin A, bioactive antioxidants, and regulatory electrolytes, which collectively support retinal integrity, mitochondrial efficiency, and systemic immunological defense.
macroIntro: A clean, low-lipid carbohydrate blueprint characterized by high-volume satiety and negligible caloric impact.
microIntro: A profound bioavailable matrix of carotenoids and electrolytes that facilitate cellular detoxification and vascular stabilization.

healthBenefits: Ocular Protection: Synergistic carotenoid yields (Beta-Carotene, Lutein) mitigate oxidative blue-light damage to retinal tissues.
Glycemic Stability: High complex fiber content delays gastric emptying, promoting stable glucose kinetics.
Vascular Support: Potassium-rich profile assists in arterial tension reduction and systemic blood pressure management.
Dermal Barrier Integrity: Provitamin A promotes accelerated mucous membrane repair and efficient epidermal cell turnover.
precautionsIntro: Nutritional precision is required for specialized metabolic conditions:
precautions: Thermal Degradation: High-heat, prolonged roasting increases the glycemic index via starch-to-sugar conversion; steam-cooking is preferred for insulin-resistant individuals.
Electrolyte Load: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) or those on potassium-sparing agents must calibrate intake to avoid hyperkalemia.
Gastrointestinal Tolerance: High fiber density may cause transient flatulence in individuals with sensitive digestive architecture or IBS.
